# FocusIDE: full documentation

> FocusIDE is a free, open source (GPL 3.0) desktop app for working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI. It shows a plan before any file changes, marks files the agent changes outside the plan while it works, and undoes a whole turn with one key. It runs on your machine with no server, no account and no telemetry.

- Website: https://yobotn.github.io/focuside/
- Source: https://github.com/yobotn/focuside
- Download: https://github.com/yobotn/focuside/releases/latest
- License: GPL 3.0
- Current version: 0.1.0
- Platforms: Windows 10 and 11 (installer, updates itself). macOS and Linux build from source.
- Publisher: yobotn (independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic)

## What FocusIDE is

FocusIDE is an IDE where the conversation with the coding agent is the center of the window. The user reads, approves and checks. The agent types. Files, diffs and a terminal are there to check the work.

FocusIDE does not include a model or an agent. The installer does include the claude-agent-acp adapter executable (Apache-2.0 source; it embeds Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK). It starts the agent the user already installed, and talks to it over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP, https://agentclientprotocol.com). Usage is billed by the agent's provider to the user's own account.

**Chat mode with Claude needs an API key or a cloud provider.** FocusIDE's chat mode connects to Claude Code through an adapter built on the Claude Agent SDK, and Anthropic asks apps built on the SDK to use API key authentication. So chat mode starts Claude with an API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, from the [Claude Console](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys)) or a cloud provider (Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry). With a Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise), run Claude in the terminal: FocusIDE opens the terminal drawer, and the user types `claude` there. Claude Code then runs with its own login. A Claude pane in FocusIDE is planned for a later version. FocusIDE never reads or stores credentials. See [Anthropic's rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use).

## Core ideas

### Plan first

With "Plan first" on (the default for agents that have a plan mode), every request first produces a plan card:

- At most 6 steps.
- Every file the agent will create, edit or delete, with a short reason.
- One line of risk.

The user can run the plan (Ctrl+Enter), revise it with a follow-up message, or discard it. Nothing changes on disk until the plan runs. While the plan runs, edits inside the plan go through without a permission prompt. Shell commands keep the agent's normal permission rules. Files tick off as the agent edits them.

### Scope guard

While the agent works, FocusIDE compares every file it touches with the plan. A file outside the plan shows up live in amber, marked "Not in plan", with a Pause button. Pause stops the turn and keeps the work so far; Continue resumes it.

### Undo turn

Before each turn, FocusIDE takes a snapshot of the project in a private git repo stored in the app's data folder. The user's own repo, branches, index and history are never touched, and the project does not need to be a git repo.

After the turn, the changes card lists every changed file with added and removed line counts. From there:

- Review opens the diff viewer (J and K step through files).
- Revert file restores one file from the snapshot.
- Undo turn (U) restores every file the agent changed to its exact bytes and removes files it created. Files the user saved during the turn are kept by default. The agent is told that the user reverted its changes.
- Redo last undo is in the command palette.

Snapshots skip nested git repos, symlinks and files over 20 MB, and the changes card says so when that matters.

### Waiting queue

Several projects stay open in a rail on the left, each with several sessions. A session waits when it has a plan to review, a permission request, or a finished or failed turn. Ctrl+J lists every waiting session across all projects. The window title shows the count. A system notification appears when a session in the background needs an answer.

## Agents

| Agent | How FocusIDE starts it |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | The bundled claude-agent-acp adapter with `--hide-claude-auth`, which runs the user's own installed `claude` binary |
| Codex | `codex-acp` (`npm install -g @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`) |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini --acp` |
| OpenCode | `opencode acp` |
| Qwen Code | `qwen --acp --experimental-skills` |
| Goose | `goose acp` |
| Custom command | Any command line that speaks ACP over stdio. Leading NAME=value parts set environment variables |

Settings shows which agents are installed. The command palette offers "New session with <agent>" for each installed agent. Each session remembers its agent, so resuming it uses the same one. Plan first is turned off for agents that do not report a plan mode; those prompts run directly, and Undo turn still works.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (x64) for the installer.
- An agent, installed and set up by the user. For Claude Code: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, plus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a cloud provider for chat mode. With a Claude plan, run `claude` in the terminal (see above).
- Git on PATH. Undo turn uses it for snapshots.

## Getting started

1. Install and set up your agent (for Claude chat mode: an API key or a cloud provider).
2. Download the installer from https://github.com/yobotn/focuside/releases/latest and run it.
3. Open a project folder (Open folder, drag a folder onto the window, or `FocusIDE.exe <folder>` from a terminal).
4. Type a request with Plan first on. Review the plan card.
5. Press Ctrl+Enter to run it. Watch the scope guard. Review the changes card. Press U to undo the turn if you do not want it.

## Keyboard shortcuts

Ctrl is Cmd on macOS.

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl+K | Command palette |
| Ctrl+P | Open a file |
| Ctrl+Shift+F | Search in the project |
| Ctrl+Enter | Run the waiting plan |
| Ctrl+. | Stop the running turn |
| Ctrl+J | Waiting queue, across projects |
| Ctrl+E | Sessions in this project |
| Ctrl+B | Show or hide the file tree |
| Ctrl+` | Show or hide the terminal |
| Ctrl+S | Save the file in the viewer |
| R / U | Review or undo a finished turn (on the changes card) |
| F | Show the full plan text (on the plan card) |
| J / K | Next or previous file in the diff viewer |
| Esc | Close an overlay or the viewer. Stops a running turn when nothing is open |

In the message box, `@` mentions a file and `/` lists the agent's commands and skills.

## Other features

- Stop (Ctrl+.) cancels the turn and ends every process the agent started, including long shell commands.
- If the agent process dies, the session shows "Agent stopped. Resume" and resumes with its history.
- Sessions are named from the first request, can be renamed, and are listed per project (Ctrl+E).
- Model picker and context usage in the top bar.
- File tree with file type icons, ignored files hidden by default.
- Viewer for code (CodeMirror) with save, and a diff viewer.
- Markdown files render as documents: tables, task lists, GitHub alerts, collapsible sections, images in the project, front matter, links between files.
- Terminal drawer that opens in the project folder (PowerShell on Windows, the login shell elsewhere).
- Resizable panels. The file tree and the viewer can sit on either side. Layout is saved.
- Light, dark or system theme. Font size setting.
- Automatic updates on Windows, from GitHub releases. Updates are signed.
- Report an issue from the app. It opens a GitHub issue with the app version and OS filled in.

## Privacy and security

- No server, no account, no telemetry, no analytics.
- FocusIDE never reads, stores or proxies agent credentials. Sign-in happens in the agent's own flow, in a terminal.
- The agent talks to its own provider exactly as it does in a terminal.
- Snapshots live in the app's data folder on the user's machine.
- Markdown from the agent and from files is sanitized before it is shown. Web images in markdown files are not loaded.
- Security problems: https://github.com/yobotn/focuside/security/advisories/new

## How it is built

- Tauri 2 and Rust: app shell, ACP client (JSON-RPC over stdio), process trees (Job Objects on Windows, process groups on Unix), shadow git snapshots, file watcher, PTY terminal.
- Svelte 5, Tailwind 4, CodeMirror 6, xterm.js, markdown-it with DOMPurify, Shiki for code blocks.
- Build from source: Rust stable, Node 22+, git. `npm run setup`, `node scripts/fetch-adapter.mjs`, `npm run dev`. `npm run build` makes the installer for the current OS.

## FAQ

**What is FocusIDE?**
A free, open source desktop app for working with AI coding agents. It shows a plan before any file changes, marks files the agent changes outside the plan, and can undo a whole turn with one key.

**Is FocusIDE free?**
Yes, GPL 3.0. You pay only for your agent, under your own plan with its provider.

**Which AI agents does it work with?**
Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Goose, and any ACP agent through a custom command.

**Does FocusIDE see my code or credentials?**
No. It runs locally, has no server, and never reads, stores or proxies credentials.

**Does my project need to be a git repo?**
No. Snapshots use a separate private repo.

**How is this different from an editor with an AI chat panel?**
The agent conversation is the main view, and the tools around it are for checking: plan before changes, live scope check, one-key undo of a whole turn, and a queue of sessions that wait for you across projects.

**Which operating systems are supported?**
Windows 10 and 11 today. macOS and Linux build from source and get installers later.

**Is FocusIDE made by Anthropic?**
No. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic. Other agent names are trademarks of their owners.
